Tariff refunds:
who gets the cash?

lines.text: Target booked about $1.3 billion in tariff refunds.
lines.say: Target booked about one point three billion dollars in tariff refunds.

lines.text: Stores often pass tariff costs to shoppers. So do you get a cut?
lines.say: Stores often pass tariff costs to shoppers. So do you get a cut?

lines.text: The Supreme Court struck down the emergency tariffs. Importers paid about $166 billion, and refunds are flowing back.
lines.say: The Supreme Court struck down the emergency tariffs. Importers paid about one hundred sixty-six billion dollars, and refunds are flowing back.

lines.text: That $1.3 billion is our math: $994 million last quarter, plus $301 million now.
lines.say: That one point three billion is our math: nine hundred ninety-four million last quarter, plus three hundred one million now.

lines.text: That added 50 cents to Target's $2.65 per share.
lines.say: That added fifty cents to Target's two dollars and sixty-five cents per share.

lines.text: To be fair, total sales still rose 7.1%.
lines.say: To be fair, Target's total sales still rose seven point one percent.

lines.text: But only importers and their customs brokers can file for a refund. Shoppers who paid higher prices can't.
lines.say: But only importers and their customs brokers can file for a refund. Shoppers who paid higher prices can't.

lines.text: One bright spot: paid a duty fee on a package? FedEx and UPS say they'll refund you once customs pays them.
lines.say: One bright spot: if you paid a duty fee on a package, FedEx and UPS say they'll refund you once customs pays them.

post.title: Target booked $1.3B in tariff refunds. Do shoppers get any?
post.ig:
Target has booked about $1.3 billion in tariff refunds over two quarters (our math: $994M in Q2 + $301M in Q3).
Q3 (reported Nov 18): $301M pretax refund benefit, adding $0.50 to EPS of $2.65.
Net sales still rose 7.1% to about $27.1B.
Importers paid about $166B in the struck-down emergency tariffs, and refunds are flowing back to them. Shoppers can't file. FedEx and UPS say they'll pass duty-fee refunds to customers once CBP pays them.
Sources: Target Q3 and Q2 releases, CBP court filings, CBS News.
